title: Antiderivatives
keyIdea: Integration reverses differentiation: add one to the power, divide by the new power, and add + C.

kid: Differentiating takes a curve and gives its gradient. An antiderivative goes the other way: you know the gradient, and you find the curve.
For a power of x, add one to the power, then divide by the new power. So x² becomes x³ ÷ 3. Always add + C at the end, because a number on its own would vanish when you differentiate.
adult: ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1) + C for every n except −1. Work term by term and keep any number in front: ∫6x² dx = 2x³ + C.
Check an answer by differentiating it: you should get back what you started with. The + C stands for a whole family of curves, each one a vertical shift of the others.

familyTip: Play 'reverse it': one person says a derivative like 6x², the other gives a curve that has it, then both check by differentiating.

practice.explain: Any constant has derivative 0, so we cannot tell which constant was there: we write + C.

pool.prompt: F(x) = x³ + {c}x is an antiderivative of f(x). Find f(2).
pool.hint: f is the derivative of F.
Add one to −2, then divide by the new power.

pool.prompt: What number goes in front of x² in ∫ ({=2*a}x + {b}) dx?
pool.explain: {=2*a}x integrates to {a}x², so the number is {a}.

visual.caption: Every curve y = x² + C has gradient 2x. Slide C: the curve moves, but its gradient at x = 1 never changes.
